O texto dos prompts não é reproduzido no artigo. Os prompts principais foram elaborados com auxílio de IA (o pesquisador forneceu o contexto do problema e a IA ajudou a estruturar o prompt); o estudo não descreve busca ou seleção automática do prompt, por isso não se atribui otimizacao_prompt. O prompt é mantido constante entre as condições: é variável de controle, não objeto de investigação, e não há condição sem ele.

riscos.descricao: GPT-4.1 ocasionalmente produziu código incompleto, exigindo prompts de acompanhamento, e teve dificuldade em tarefas complexas de depuração, ficando às vezes preso em ciclos repetitivos de soluções ineficazes.

A geração de código não esteve livre de erros menores, e o critério de sucesso foi a execução bem-sucedida de testes unitários gerados pela própria IA, que podem não capturar todos os aspectos dos requisitos iniciais.

riscos.descricao: Segurança operacional da execução, não cibersegurança: Claude 3.7 às vezes gerava, depois de verificada toda a funcionalidade, novos casos de teste desnecessários que introduziam falhas, e o pesquisador precisava interromper o processo à força para evitar a corrupção do projeto.

heterogeneidade.descricao: Aparente inconsistência entre o rótulo e os valores da média: o estudo chama de «average task completion time» cerca de 1,5 minuto (GPT-4.1) e mais de 3 minutos (Claude 3.7), mas relata totais de cerca de 58 e 137 minutos em 12 tarefas. citacoes.trecho: This study aims to quantitatively compare the efficiency of the GPT-4.1 and Claude 3.7 Sonnet AI models using GitHub Copilot in Agent Mode, with a case study focused on developing a backend REST API application.
Independent Variable: The AI model used (GPT-4.1 or Claude 3.7 Sonnet).
Prompts were categorized into two types: a main prompt to initiate feature creation and follow-up prompts for corrections or refinements.
The main prompts were crafted with assistance from AI: the researcher provided the core problem context, and the AI helped structure a more comprehensive and effective prompt.
This main prompt, identical for both models in each task, typically included: project context, feature specifications, implementation steps, technical constraints, and logging requirements.
Follow-up prompts were necessarily adaptive, responding to the specific code generated by the model.
Initial Prompt: Give the main prompt to the selected AI model to generate the necessary code and corresponding unit tests.
If it does not meet requirements or if unit tests fail, use follow-up prompts to correct the code.
It is important to acknowledge that this measure is not purely AI processing time, as it includes user-incurred delays (e.g., time taken to confirm a command-line execution).
Context Isolation: To prevent context from a previous task from influencing the next one, a new chat session was initiated for each new feature being developed.
The final quantitative metrics for GPT 4.1 utilized data collected by both developers.
Overall, GPT-4.1 required fewer prompts (38) compared to Claude 3.7 (44).
GPT-4.1 had an average task completion time of approximately 1.5 minutes, whereas Claude 3.7 averaged over 3 minutes.
The total cumulative time starkly highlights this difference: GPT-4.1 completed all tasks in approximately 58 minutes, while Claude 3.7 required 137 minutes.
Weaknesses: Occasionally produced incomplete code, requiring follow-up prompts.
It also struggled with complex debugging tasks, sometimes getting stuck in ineffective, repetitive solution loops.
Over-engineering: Sometimes provided excessive code.

On occasion, after all functionality was verified, it would generate new, unnecessary test cases that introduced failures, requiring the researcher to forcibly stop the process to prevent project corruption.

citacoes.trecho: Analysis of the data reveals that the second developer utilized a higher number of prompts than the main developer.
citacoes.localizador: PDF p. 6, texto após a Figura 3

citacoes.trecho: The experiment showed that GPT-4.1 required six fewer prompts than Claude 3.7 Sonnet and was significantly faster, with cumulative time savings of approximately 78 minutes.

Potential Researcher Bias: The evaluation process, particularly the formulation of follow-up prompts and the counting methodology, may contain subjective elements, although every effort was made to maintain objectivity.
Therefore, the success criterion for a task was primarily determined by the successful execution of AI-generated unit tests, which may not capture all aspects of the initial requirements perfectly.

citacoes.trecho: The conclusion of this study shows a correlation between generation speed and the model used for code generation.
